notes: Type `clip`, a space and text in the palette to search your clipboard history, whether or not it shows in the main search.

A text-reading hiccup on an image is retried instead of marking it as having no text, and saving copies, text reading and the day counts write less often.

When older pins are unpinned to keep the history within its storage, a notice says how many and why.

io.navbytes.stackbar.clipboard.description:
Everything you copy, searchable, pinnable and one keystroke from being pasted
back. ⌘⇧V opens it in the palette from anywhere, with a preview of the
selected copy beside the list: type to filter, ↑↓ and Return (or ⌘1 to ⌘9)
to paste into the app you were in, ⌥Return to paste as plain text, ⌘P to pin
and ⌥⌫ to delete. Formatted text keeps its formatting, and images are kept by
the host and pasted back. The text in a copied image (a screenshot, a
photo of a receipt) is read on your Mac, so typing finds the image, and ⌘⇧T
copies that text. ⌘K holds every action, Pause Recording and Ignore Next
Copy included. The popup with the last copy and the Pause buttons is still on
the menu bar icon, if you turn the icon on.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the clipboard. Passwords are skipped: the host never hands out items an app marks as concealed or transient, and copies from password managers (or any app you add) are ignored. Copies that look like secrets (API keys and tokens, JSON web tokens, private keys, card numbers, six-digit codes) are shown masked, kept out of agent tools, and dropped after 15 minutes unless you pin them.

**Tab** (Stackbar 0.36 and later; you can change what Tab does in Settings ›
Command Palette), or pick **Ask AI** under the results for any text. Type

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.git-sync.description:
Which of your local git repositories are behind their remote, ahead of it,
diverged or holding uncommitted changes, in the menu bar, with the safe
ones updated in one click. Worktrees show under their repository, and the
merged ones left behind are cleaned up in one go.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `git` and `find` (Stackbar finds them in `/usr/bin` or Homebrew and asks you to approve those paths once), your SSH agent for remotes over SSH, and to open folders in your editor, terminal or Finder. It never reads your files itself: git runs only in the folders you choose, and each plugin's Settings page lists them with Remove. Needs Stackbar 0.35.0 or later, and git (the Xcode Command Line Tools or Homebrew's).

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar (only when something is behind, by default), panel, window, widget, settings.

facts.label: How it checks
facts.text: it finds the repositories in your folders (2 levels deep by default; skipping `node_modules`, `.build`, `Pods` and the like), and reads each with `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` every two minutes, which uses no network. `git fetch --prune --no-tags` runs every 15 minutes per repository, a few repositories a minute, and on wake; it never changes your files. Prompts are off, so a remote that wants a password says so instead of waiting.

facts.label: Updating
facts.text: Pull is fast-forward only (or rebase, in Settings), so it never makes a merge commit. A repository with uncommitted changes is skipped, or stashed, pulled and restored, or offered on its row, as you choose; if restoring conflicts, your changes stay in the stash. io.navbytes.stackbar.pr-cockpit.description:
Your pull requests and the ones waiting on your review, with CI, review state
and merge conflicts, in the menu bar; the issues assigned to you; and your
repositories and new issues from the palette. It tells you when someone asks
for your review, when an issue is assigned to you, and when one of your own
pull requests is approved, gets changes requested, or fails its checks.

uninstall it: its repositories, assigned issues and Create GitHub Issue are
all here, with the same `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

facts.label: Needs

Approving, merging, auto-merge and Mark Ready for Review need write access to pull requests (merging also needs contents write). Mark as done in the inbox needs notifications. On GitHub Enterprise Server, turn it on in Settings and enter the server as `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_URL`; the plugin then reaches that server and no other.

facts.label: Checks on click

In the palette, a selected pull request shows its checks beside the list, fetched in the background for the ones whose checks changed (a setting turns this off); ⌘I opens them in full.
